{"sql":"SELECT
  g.GenreId,
  g.Name AS Genre,
  COALESCE(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 0.0) AS revenue,
  COALESCE(SUM(il.Quantity), 0) AS units_sold,
  ROUND(AVG(t.UnitPrice),2) AS avg_track_list_price
FROM Genre g
LEFT JOIN Track t ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name
ORDER BY revenue DESC;"}

SELECT
  g.GenreId,
  g.Name AS Genre,
  COALESCE(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 0.0) AS revenue,
  COALESCE(SUM(il.Quantity), 0) AS units_sold,
  ROUND(AVG(t.UnitPrice),2) AS avg_track_list_price
FROM Genre g
LEFT JOIN Track t ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name
ORDER BY revenue DESC;
assumptions: I used the standard definition profit margin = (revenue - cost) / revenue. To compute this requires a cost or COGS value per track or per genre, which is not present in any table.
